# pbs_prune_job (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server prune job: on a schedule, it removes the backups of a datastore, or of a namespace in it, that its retention options do not keep. Each backup group — the backups of one VM, container or host — is pruned on its own. The space the removed backups held is freed by the datastore's garbage collection, `gc_schedule` of `pbs_datastore`.

PBS goes through the options in order — `last`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly` — and a backup that one of them keeps is not counted again by the next. A backup that none keeps is removed, unless it is protected.

Deleting a datastore without `keep_job_configs` deletes its prune jobs too; a `pbs_prune_job` then plans to create its job again. Managing prune jobs needs `Datastore.Modify` on the datastore, reading them `Datastore.Audit`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The retention of a datastore lives in its prune jobs. This one prunes
# pbs_datastore.store1, of the pbs_datastore example, assumed in the same
# configuration; referring to its name creates the job after the datastore.
resource "pbs_prune_job" "store1" {
  id       = "daily-store1"
  store    = pbs_datastore.store1.name
  schedule = "daily"
  comment  = "Retention of cluster1's backups"

  # In each backup group, the backups of one guest: the 3 most recent
  # backups, then the last backup of each of 7 more days, 4 more weeks and 6
  # more months. A backup one option keeps is not counted again by the next.
  keep = {
    last    = 3
    daily   = 7
    weekly  = 4
    monthly = 6
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Job ID, 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Changing it replaces the job.
- `keep` (Attributes) Retention: how many backups of each kind to keep, at least one kind. A kind left out keeps no backups for its own sake. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--keep))
- `schedule` (String) When the job runs, as a PBS calendar event such as `daily`, `hourly`, `sat 03:00` or `mon..fri *:00/30`. PBS checks it.
- `store` (String) Name of the datastore to prune, such as the `name` of a `pbs_datastore`.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `disable` (Boolean) Whether the job is disabled: it keeps its settings but does not run. Defaults to `false`.
- `max_depth` (Number) How many levels of namespaces below `ns` to prune too, from `0`, `ns` alone, to `7`; all of them when left out. Namespaces nest at most 7 levels deep, and PBS goes no deeper than that below `ns`.
- `ns` (String) Namespace to prune, such as `dept1` or `dept1/hosts`; the datastore's root namespace when left out.

<a id="nestedatt--keep"></a>
### Nested Schema for `keep`

Optional:

- `daily` (Number) How many backups to keep that are the last backup of each of the most recent days.
- `hourly` (Number) How many backups to keep that are the last backup of each of the most recent hours.
- `last` (Number) How many backups to keep that are the most recent backups.
- `monthly` (Number) How many backups to keep that are the last backup of each of the most recent months.
- `weekly` (Number) How many backups to keep that are the last backup of each of the most recent weeks, which start on Monday.
- `yearly` (Number) How many backups to keep that are the last backup of each of the most recent years.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_prune_job.store1
  identity = {
    id = "daily-store1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Job ID, such as `daily-store1`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_prune_job.store1
  id = "daily-store1"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Prune jobs are imported by job ID, as `proxmox-backup-manager prune-job
# list` shows it.
terraform import pbs_prune_job.store1 daily-store1
```
